facts.text: Lyndeborough was first granted a charter in 1734 as Salem-Canada, a delayed payment to Salem, Massachusetts veterans of the 1690 Canada expedition.
The town became the Town of Lyndeborough in 1764, named for Benjamin Lynde, Jr., a prominent Salem judge.
The Lyndeborough Glass Factory operated in South Lyndeborough from 1866 to 1886, producing some of the finest glass in northern New England.
Citizens' Hall, opened in 1889, now sits on the National Register of Historic Places and houses the Lafayette Artillery Company.
The highest point in Lyndeborough is just shy of 1,800 feet where the east ridge of North Pack Monadnock Mountain crosses the town's western border.
Peter Clark’s Pottery produced popular red ware in North Lyndeborough for at least two generations before moving to Concord before 1900.
